channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: UK and EU Erasmus+ youth exchanges to start in mid-2027
item.description: While the previous Erasmus scheme was focused on university mobility exchanges, Erasmus+ allows shorter exchanges of a few days.

item.title: Death toll rises to 68 following high-speed rail crash near Madrid
item.description: At least 64 people were killed in a train crash on Wednesday morning in Urda, about 100 kilometres south of Madrid, a spokesperson for the Castile-La Mancha regional government said.

item.title: EU to introduce extra fee on small parcels coming into the bloc
item.description: The European Union will introduce a €2 handling fee on small parcels ordered outside of the bloc from 1 November.

item.title: Netherlands confirms non-participation in Eurovision Song Contest 2027
item.description: Despite the non-participation, broadcaster NOS will still show the contest in the Netherlands, including with Dutch commentary.

item.title: UK Prime Minister sets out red lines on free movement ahead of November EU summit
item.description: He suggested that Labour’s next election campaign, expected in 2029, could include a pledge to rejoin the EU.

item.title: Six Belgian cities among most tourist-oriented cities in the world
item.description: Bruges and five other Belgian cities also made it into the top 100 of the most tourist-oriented cities in the world, according to a study published by One Street Back.

item.title: Psoriasis Day aims to break down taboos around rare skin disease
item.description: Symptoms are often mistaken for irritation, thrush or an STI, delaying proper treatment. Campaigners say the taboo around intimate psoriasis has become a wider societal issue.

item.title: FIFA president confident to stay in power amid scandals
item.description: Gianni Infantino has faced criticism for several radical steps throughout his presidency, but continues to enjoy support from national associations.

item.title: More than 800 'gilets jaunes' protests expected in France on Saturday
item.description: The protests come as the Council of Europe has called on governments to safeguard freedom of peaceful assembly and ensure that police operations comply with human rights.

item.title: US intelligence chief warns of Iranian attacks targeting American citizens
item.description: The US had previously ordered non-essential personnel to leave the Gulf before the start of its war with Iran, and again in July before President Donald Trump called off another wave of strikes.

item.title: Belgium switches to winter time tonight: Why are we still changing the clocks?
item.description: Belgians will gain an extra hour of sleep this weekend as the country switches to winter time in the early hours of Sunday 25 October.

item.title: One dead, four injured in Paris-area shooting; police probe racist or religious motive
item.description: One person was killed and four others, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded after a man opened fire in Trappes and La Verrière, west of Paris, on Friday morning.

item.title: Ukraine still reports issues with Starshield, despite Trump announcing restoration of access
item.description: Ukraine’s military still faces restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite communications system.

item.title: Hot summer claimed the lives of more than 50,000 Europeans
item.description: The extreme heat last summer has claimed the lives of more than 50,000 people in Europe, according to a new study.

item.title: PHP Warns: Outdated websites remain vulnerable to attacks
item.description: Websites running on outdated versions of PHP remain vulnerable unless they are updated, the PHP Foundation has warned.

item.title: ‘I stayed in emergency mode’: How Iranian students in Belgium grapple with the ongoing war
item.description: While internet access in Iran has been partially restored and the protests have been crushed, the crisis hasn’t ended for Iranian students in Belgium.

item.title: France to deploy military in support of police ahead of fresh protests
item.description: France will tighten security on Saturday, deploying soldiers to support police ahead of fresh protests, while all demonstrations have been banned in Lyon.

item.title: ‘Overshoot is not surrender’: UN issues strong warnings ahead of climate change summit
item.description: “Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5°C increases climate impacts and risks."

item.title: Belgian Foreign Minister condemns alliance between former Congo leader and M23 rebels
item.description: Maxime Prévot has condemned the alliance between the former President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Joseph Kabila, and the M23 rebel movement.

item.title: PM De Wever 'certain' European Commission will not reopen debate on Russian assets
item.description: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever (NV-A) said he is certain the European Commission will not reopen the debate over using frozen Russian assets held at Euroclear to help finance Ukraine.
